Expand along the first row, using the signs $+,-,+$. Compute the three signed contributions separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{1} & =(1 - 2 p)\begin{vmatrix}3 & 0 \\ -2 & 2\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(1 - 2 p)((3)(2)-(0)(-2)) \\  & =(1 - 2 p)(6) \\  & =6 - 12 p\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{2} & =-(5)\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 5 & 2\end{vmatrix} \\  & =-(5)((1)(2)-(0)(5)) \\  & =-(5)(2) \\  & =-10\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{3} & =(2 p + 1)\begin{vmatrix}1 & 3 \\ 5 & -2\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(2 p + 1)((1)(-2)-(3)(5)) \\  & =(2 p + 1)(-17) \\  & =- 34 p - 17\end{aligned}
$$

Add the signed contributions to obtain the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =T_1+T_2+T_3 \\  & =- 46 p - 21\end{aligned}
$$

Set the determinant equal to the given value.

$$
\begin{aligned}- 46 p - 21 & =-38 \\ - 46 p & =-17 \\ p & =\frac{17}{46}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $p=\frac{17}{46}$.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-x_{1}-x_{2}+x_{3} &=-1 \\ -x_{1}-2x_{2}+x_{3} &=2 \\ x_{1}+x_{2}-x_{3} &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use Gaussian elimination to reduce its augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-1 & -1 & 1 & -1 \\ -1 & -2 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & -1 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply Gaussian elimination to every augmented column:

$$
\begin{aligned}M &=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-1 & -1 & 1 & -1 \\ -1 & -2 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & -1 & 1\end{array}\right] \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & -1 & 1\end{array}\right]\qquad R_{1}\gets -1R_{1} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & -1 & 1\end{array}\right]\qquad R_{2}\gets R_{2}+(1)R_{1} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]\qquad R_{3}\gets R_{3}+(-1)R_{1} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]\qquad R_{2}\gets -1R_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus a row echelon form is

$$
M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The final row is the redundant equation $0=0$; there are two coefficient pivots.

Keeping the columns in the order $x,y,z$, the augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & 4 & -8 & -6 \\ -2 & 4 & -8 & -6 \\ -3 & 6 & -12 & -9\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1\leftarrow \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 4 & 3 \\ -2 & 4 & -8 & -6 \\ -3 & 6 & -12 & -9\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_2\leftarrow R_2-(-2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 6 & -12 & -9\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_3\leftarrow R_3-(-3)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

There is one pivot. The two zero rows express $0=0$, so they impose no restrictions. The **basic variable** is $x$; the **free variables** are $y,z$. The remaining equation and its rearrangement are

$$
\begin{aligned}x-2y+4z &=3 \\ x &=3+2y-4z\end{aligned}
$$

Thus all solutions are

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3+2y-4z \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix},\quad y,z\in\mathbb{R}
$$

Separating the constant part and the contributions of the two free variables gives

$$

The two free parameters range independently over all real numbers, so the solution set is a plane.

question.:question/problem:
Find all real values of $p$ for which the following matrix is singular.

$$
\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & 2 \\ - 3 p - 4 & 4 p + 7 & - 3 p - 3 \\ - 5 p - 8 & 6 p + 13 & - 5 p - 9\end{bmatrix}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Expand along the first row, using the signs $+,-,+$. Compute the three signed contributions separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{1} & =(1)\begin{vmatrix}4 p + 7 & - 3 p - 3 \\ 6 p + 13 & - 5 p - 9\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(1)((4 p + 7)(- 5 p - 9)-(- 3 p - 3)(6 p + 13)) \\  & =(1)(- 2 p^{2} - 14 p - 24) \\  & =- 2 p^{2} - 14 p - 24\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{2} & =-(-2)\begin{vmatrix}- 3 p - 4 & - 3 p - 3 \\ - 5 p - 8 & - 5 p - 9\end{vmatrix} \\  & =-(-2)((- 3 p - 4)(- 5 p - 9)-(- 3 p - 3)(- 5 p - 8)) \\  & =-(-2)(8 p + 12) \\  & =16 p + 24\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{3} & =(2)\begin{vmatrix}- 3 p - 4 & 4 p + 7 \\ - 5 p - 8 & 6 p + 13\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(2)((- 3 p - 4)(6 p + 13)-(4 p + 7)(- 5 p - 8)) \\  & =(2)(2 p^{2} + 4 p + 4) \\  & =4 p^{2} + 8 p + 8\end{aligned}
$$

Add the signed contributions to obtain the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =T_1+T_2+T_3 \\  & =2 p^{2} + 10 p + 8\end{aligned}
$$

A singular matrix has determinant $0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}2 p^{2} + 10 p + 8 & =0 \\ 2 (p + 1) (p + 4) & =0 \\ p & =-4,\,-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $p=-4$ and $p=-1$.

$$

A singular matrix has determinant $0$.

\begin{aligned}1 - p & =0 \\ - p & =-1 \\ p & =1\end{aligned}

$$

$$

Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y+z+w &=2 \\ x+2y-z-3w &=4 \\ 2x+4y-2w &=6\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the system. Select the general solution in the variable order $x,y,z,w$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix, with columns in the stated variable order, is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 & -3 & 4 \\ 2 & 4 & 0 & -2 & 6\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_2\leftarrow R_2-R_1$:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -4 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 & 0 & -2 & 6\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_3\leftarrow R_3-2R_1$:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -4 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_2\leftarrow -\frac12 R_2$:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -4 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_3\leftarrow R_3+2R_2$:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_1\leftarrow R_1-R_2$:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

This is reduced row echelon form. The zero row represents $0=0$ and imposes no restriction. The pivots are in the $x$ and $z$ columns, so both $y$ and $w$ are free. The nonzero rows give

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y-w &=3 \\ z+2w &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Solving for the pivot variables gives $x=3-2y+w$ and $z=-1-2w$. Thus the general solution is

$$
\begin{bmatrix}3-2y+w \\ y \\ -1-2w \\ w\end{bmatrix},\quad y,w\in\mathbb{R}
$$

The values of $y$ and $w$ can be chosen independently. Substitution into the three original left-hand sides gives $2$, $4$, and $6$, respectively, for every pair of real values. Conversely, every solution must satisfy the two pivot equations, so this vector includes all solutions. Setting $w=y$ would omit solutions; for example, $(4,0,-3,1)$ is a solution with different values of $w$ and $y$. A single vector such as $(3,0,-1,0)$ is only one solution.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x-2y+4z+4w &=-14 \\ -2x+5y-7z-7w &=11 \\ -2x+3y-3z-5w &=9.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}2 & -2 & 4 & 4 & -14 \\ -2 & 5 & -7 & -7 & 11 \\ -2 & 3 & -3 & -5 & 9\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}2 & -2 & 4 & 4 & -14 \\ -2 & 5 & -7 & -7 & 11 \\ -2 & 3 & -3 & -5 & 9\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 & -7 \\ -2 & 5 & -7 & -7 & 11 \\ -2 & 3 & -3 & -5 & 9\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 & -7 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -3 & -3 \\ -2 & 3 & -3 & -5 & 9\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 & -7 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 & -5\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 & -7 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 & -5\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 & -7 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 & -4\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 & -7 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & -2\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 & -7 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & -2\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & -2\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & -2\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+w &=-6 \\ y-w &=-3 \\ z &=-2.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y$ and $z$, and we have one free variable, $w$. That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ and $z$ in terms of $w$.

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-w-6 \\ y &=w-3 \\ z &=-2 \\ w &=w,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $w$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z \\ w\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-w-6 \\ w-3 \\ -2 \\ w\end{bmatrix},\,w\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x-4y+4z-10w &=4 \\ -x+5y-5z+8w &=4 \\ -2x+6y-4z+8w &=-8.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}2 & -4 & 4 & -10 & 4 \\ -1 & 5 & -5 & 8 & 4 \\ -2 & 6 & -4 & 8 & -8\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}2 & -4 & 4 & -10 & 4 \\ -1 & 5 & -5 & 8 & 4 \\ -2 & 6 & -4 & 8 & -8\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -5 & 2 \\ -1 & 5 & -5 & 8 & 4 \\ -2 & 6 & -4 & 8 & -8\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -5 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & 3 & 6 \\ -2 & 6 & -4 & 8 & -8\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -5 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & -2 & -4\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -5 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & -2 & -4\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -5 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -4 & -8\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -5 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 & -4\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -5 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 & -4\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & -2 & 0 & -1 & 10 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 & -4\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 0 & 0 & -3 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 & -4\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-3w &=6 \\ y-w &=-2 \\ z-2w &=-4.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y$ and $z$, and we have one free variable, $w$. That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ and $z$ in terms of $w$.

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=3w+6 \\ y &=w-2 \\ z &=2w-4 \\ w &=w,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $w$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z \\ w\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3w+6 \\ w-2 \\ 2w-4 \\ w\end{bmatrix},\,w\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x+4y-2z-2w &=-4 \\ -2x-y+5z-10w &=1 \\ -x-4y+z+5w &=6.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}2 & 4 & -2 & -2 & -4 \\ -2 & -1 & 5 & -10 & 1 \\ -1 & -4 & 1 & 5 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}2 & 4 & -2 & -2 & -4 \\ -2 & -1 & 5 & -10 & 1 \\ -1 & -4 & 1 & 5 & 6\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & -1 & -2 \\ -2 & -1 & 5 & -10 & 1 \\ -1 & -4 & 1 & 5 & 6\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & -12 & -3 \\ -1 & -4 & 1 & 5 & 6\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & -12 & -3 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & 4 & 4\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & 4 & 4\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -4 & 2\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & -3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+w &=3 \\ y-2w &=-2 \\ z-2w &=1.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y$ and $z$, and we have one free variable, $w$. That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ and $z$ in terms of $w$.

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-w+3 \\ y &=2w-2 \\ z &=2w+1 \\ w &=w,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $w$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z \\ w\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-w+3 \\ 2w-2 \\ 2w+1 \\ w\end{bmatrix},\,w\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x+2y+2z-6w &=6 \\ 2x+5y-z-18w &=9 \\ x+3y+z-9w &=9.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}2 & 2 & 2 & -6 & 6 \\ 2 & 5 & -1 & -18 & 9 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & -9 & 9\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}2 & 2 & 2 & -6 & 6 \\ 2 & 5 & -1 & -18 & 9 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & -9 & 9\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & -3 & 3 \\ 2 & 5 & -1 & -18 & 9 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & -9 & 9\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & -3 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -12 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & -9 & 9\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & -3 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -12 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & -6 & 6\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & -3 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & -6 & 6\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & -3 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2 & 4\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & -3 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & -3 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 1 & 0 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}1 & 0 & 0 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-w &=-2 \\ y-3w &=3 \\ z+w &=2.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y$ and $z$, and we have one free variable, $w$. That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ and $z$ in terms of $w$.

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=w-2 \\ y &=3w+3 \\ z &=-w+2 \\ w &=w,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $w$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z \\ w\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}w-2 \\ 3w+3 \\ -w+2 \\ w\end{bmatrix},\,w\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x+2y-4z-16w &=18 \\ -x+2y-4z-7w &=24 \\ -2x-3y+8z+25w &=-37.\end{aligned}\right.

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-3w &=-2 \\ y-w &=3 \\ z+2w &=-4.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y$ and $z$, and we have one free variable, $w$. That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ and $z$ in terms of $w$.

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=3w-2 \\ y &=w+3 \\ z &=-2w-4 \\ w &=w,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $w$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z \\ w\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3w-2 \\ w+3 \\ -2w-4 \\ w\end{bmatrix},\,w\in (-\infty ,\infty ).

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x-2y-2z+8w &=-6 \\ -x+4y-2z-7w &=18 \\ -x+3y+z-10w &=7.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}2 & -2 & -2 & 8 & -6 \\ -1 & 4 & -2 & -7 & 18 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & -10 & 7\end{array}\right].
$$

\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & -4 & 8 & -8 \\ 2 & -1 & 8 & -5 \\ 2 & -3 & 8 & -7\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 4 & -4 \\ 2 & -1 & 8 & -5 \\ 2 & -3 & 8 & -7\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 4 & -4 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & -3 & 8 & -7\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 4 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -3 & 8 & -7\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 4 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 4 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+4z &=-2 \\ y &=1.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and we have one free variable, $z$. That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$.

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-4z-2 \\ y &=1 \\ z &=z,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-4z-2 \\ 1 \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
